articles.title: Stranger Than Heaven Studio Made The Tupac Resurrection Less Weird By Not Using AI
articles.summary: RGG Studio's Stranger Than Heaven is certainly living up to its title, as the decision to resurrect the late rapper Tupac Shakur as a character in the game was perceived as odd when it was first announced at Summer Game Fest.
body: "RGG Studio is treating this integration with the utmost respect for his legacy, crafting every aspect in close collaboration and without the use of AI, including his character design based on archival footage and photographs," the studio wrote. More details on the character who uses Shakur's likeness, Amaru, will be shared at a later date.

According to RGG Studio head Masayoshi Yokoyama, it was Snoop Dogg himself who suggested Tupac for the role. The rapper also appears in Stranger Than Heaven, where his official character description notes that he plays the globe-trotting merchant Orpheus, who has an "open mind" about the legality of his wares. In the game, Orpheus discovers that the protagonist, Daito, has stowed away aboard his ship, and he mentors him in the harsh life that awaits him on his way to 1915 Japan.

The rest of the game's cast also features a varied and talented selection of performers from across the globe, including musicians Tori Kelly and Satoshi Fujihara, Shogun actor Tokuma Nishioka, and famed voice actor Akio Otsuka. You can expect to encounter all of them throughout the game's story, which covers 50 years of history.

articles.title: 'I Don’t Think Starfield Was Anywhere Near Successful Enough to Do a Starfield 2' – Former Bethesda Dev Casts Doubt on Sequel
articles.summary: Bethesda is still hard at work on new DLC for Starfield, but you probably shouldn't expect a sequel anytime soon. Former Bethesda Lead Systems Designer Kurt Kuhlmann spoke to FRVR, and when he was asked about a potential Starfield sequel, he told the outlet: "I don’t think Starfield was anywhere…
body: That's not too surprising, as the game has been massively divisive since it came out, despite getting a mostly-positive review from us here at IGN. Our reviewer Dan Stapleton said: "Starfield has a lot of forces working against it, but eventually the allure of its expansive roleplaying quests and respectable combat make its gravitational pull difficult to resist."

Kuhlmann then goes on to reminisce on the ambition of Starfield, and how a sequel could have done something great, saying, "It’s, in a way, too bad, because I think with the lessons learned on Starfield, a Starfield 2 could have been much closer to the game that Todd [Howard] had [in mind]." Starfield has improved a lot since it first came out, and it's still has improvements down the pipeline, but it's pretty clear that it fell short of Todd Howard's ambitions ahead of its release.

articles.title: Warhammer 40,000 Space Marine 2's New Class Is Finally Confirmed — and It's Exactly What Everyone Suspected
articles.summary: Big news for Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine 2 fans today: publisher Focus Entertainment has revealed the game’s Year 3 roadmap and confirmed the new class set to hit early 2027. Let’s get straight to the headline here: the new class is — as so many had suspected — the Apothecary.
body: “We’ve been following all your speculations ever since we teased the arrival of a new class, and you certainly had plenty of theories… and the majority of you were right!” Focus said. “Today, we’re finally revealing the truth: the Apothecary is joining the ranks with Patch 17 in the first quarter of 2027! We’ll disclose more info later, so stay tuned!
“Additionally, as we said in the previous Community Update, the Apothecary will receive a Champion skin in the same way the Techmarine did: in the update after its release.”

That’s all we have on the Apothecary, unfortunately, but we have plenty more on Year 3. Patch 15 hits October 1, with Patch 16 out before the end of this year. The long-awaited Chaos Siege mode, which lets you to play Heretic Astartes previously exclusive to PvP, arrives with Patch 15, as does the One-Handed Thunder Hammer. Patch 16 adds a brand-new PvP mode featuring Weekly Stratagems, just like in PvE.
2027 will being the Apothecary, as mentioned, new Operations and weapons, and “reworks to several gameplay features, with improvements coming to some of the game’s core systems,” Focus said.

articles.title: GTA 6 $400 Collector’s Edition Comes With Everything Except The Game
articles.summary: Rockstar Games has officially confirmed a $400 Grand Theft Auto 6 collector's edition, which doesn't include the game. The developer says The Goodtime State: Vice City Collection is inspired by Leonida’s hit TV show, Macca the Gator, and it's now available to preorder.
body: It's a pretty solid selection of swag, but is it worth $400? Immediate reactions online have been very critical to the price that Rockstar Games and Take-Two Interactive are charging for this box of collectibles, but as people online have pointed out, this collector's edition will likely sell out fast--and there are already eBay listings for it. Scalpers pounced on the GTA 6 DualSense controllers when they were first announced, and on eBay, they're currently selling them at a premium.

It's also not too surprising to see a collector's edition that doesn't include the video game it's based on, as several big games have opted to sell standalone merchandise bundles. Marathon, Diablo 4, and Borderlands 4 are a few notable examples, and in the case of GTA 6, Take-Two Interactive won't have to risk preorder cancellations. According to a third-party research company, GTA 6 has already generated over $400 million in revenue from preorders alone.

articles.title: Activision’s Halo Must Go Beyond Bungie
articles.summary: Xbox has struggled to recapture Bungie's Halo magic for 15 years. Activision's new game needs to give the series a Doom (2016) style rethink.
body: Of course, thanks to a $69 billion acquisition, Call of Duty is now Xbox’s Call of Duty. But I think you get the idea: Halo should be massive. It should be the premier first-person shooter on Xbox. It should be delivering stellar campaigns and phenomenal multiplayer on a regular basis. It should be among Team Green’s most-played games on any given day.

But it isn’t. And perhaps the reason why is nothing more than the passage of time and the shifting of trends. Can any game sit on the popularity throne forever? The simple truth may be that Master Chief is an artefact of the original Xbox and 360 days, and that 2010’s incredible Halo: Reach was a natural end point that should have been respected.

With this in mind, it’s entirely unsurprising to see that Xbox’s CEO, Asha Sharma, has assigned Activision the task of developing the next Halo. If nothing else, Activision is an unrelenting video game factory; a colossal machine of rotating studios that assembles high-budget shooters year in, year out. If Sharma wants to ship Halo games – lots of Halo games – there’s no better Microsoft division to rectify that issue.
points: Xbox has struggled to recapture Bungie's Halo magic for 15 years.
Activision's new game needs to give the series a Doom (2016) style rethink.
Of course, thanks to a $69 billion acquisition, Call of Duty is now Xbox’s Call of Duty.
But I think you get the idea: Halo should be massive.
articles.author: Matt Purslow

articles.title: GTA 6 Is Getting a $400 Collector's Set That Doesn't Include the Game
articles.summary: GTA 6 is getting a $400 collector's set filled with Vice City-themed goodies, but it won't include a copy of the game. Rockstar Games has announced a collector's set for GTA 6 known as GTA 6: The Goodtime State – Vice City Collection.
body: One interesting thing to note here is that previous GTA and Red Dead games have historically always included a physical map in the standard edition of the game. We've reached out to Rockstar to see if the map is included in the boxed copies of GTA 6 or if players will have to shell out a few hundred bucks to get one.

With that said, this is a pretty pricey box set, but at least the items are of high-quality. By partnering with brands like Oakley for these items, it does ensure that these aren't cheap gas station quality sunglasses that will fall apart on you in a few months. You can also likely expect that these will sell out rather quickly and be resold on eBay for absurd prices. GTA 6-themed shirts were given away at Tokyo Game Show earlier this month and have been popping up online for hundreds of dollars.

articles.title: Xbox’s New Mythic Achievements Take 15 Seconds To Tell You “Good Job”
articles.summary: Xbox Achievements have remained mostly the same since they were first introduced decades ago, but it looks like they're set to evolve slightly with the introduction of "Mythic" Achievements.
body: On the surface, it looks like adding a Mythic Achievement to your shelf is a sign that you've truly done everything there is to do in a game, so sitting back and enjoying the lengthy applause from your Xbox after you've poured hours into it makes sense.

According to TrueAchievements, Mythic Achievements are worth zero Gamerscore and are tracked separately from your usual Achievements. Xbox CEO Asha Sharma had teased the rollout of these new awards back in August, but it looks like they're rolling out during another bleak week at Xbox.

As part of ongoing cuts, hundreds of people have been laid off across Xbox Game Studios, studio consolidation has resulted in various developers being grouped under new arms of Xbox, and things are not looking good for Ninja Theory. Undead Labs has also found a new owner --that has not been officially revealed yet--but the move away from Xbox has resulted in downsizing at the State of Decay 3 developer.

articles.title: Meta’s $1,300 VR Glasses Could Be The Most Expensive Way To Play Xbox Games
articles.summary: For years, Meta has had one of the best entry-level virtual reality headsets with the Quest 3 and its slightly lower-specced successor, the Quest 3S. The VR hardware packs a punch, but if you're looking for an even lighter option, the company's new VR glasses could catch your attention.
body: According to Meta, the VR Glasses weigh just 100 grams, thanks to a pocket-sized puck that is tethered to the specs. This unit houses all the tech for running apps and games on the VR Glasses, and inside you'll find a Qualcomm Snapdragon Reality Elite chipset, 128GB of storage, 12GB of RAM, and a battery. The glasses feature 5K Micro OLED lenses, which can output 2412 x 2288 pixels per eye at a 120Hz refresh rate.

Out of the box, these can access all apps and games from the Meta Quest catalog, and they support Xbox Cloud Gaming. Meta also says that they're "IMAX-Enhanced certified" as they support the Dolby Vision HDR format, and they can be used to watch 3D movies. When they arrive, users will have a library of 75 games that they can play using only their hands, or they can connect it to a gaming console or handheld as an alternate display option. These do not come with controllers by default, but you can buy Touch Plus controllers separately or pair an existing Quest 3/3S set with the glasses.

articles.title: Age of Empires Studio’s Next Game Canceled as Part of Xbox Layoffs
articles.summary: Xbox 's ongoing layoffs are so sweeping that we’re still piecing together the full picture. In early July, the company announced it would immediately cut 1,600 employees, with more layoffs in the next fiscal year.
body: On Tuesday, Microsoft announced another wave of layoffs affecting 268 employees, as well as a major restructuring that would shift the Halo series to Activision and give Bethesda Softworks control of Obsidian Entertainment. As part of this reorganization, Activision also inherited World’s Edge, which Microsoft created in 2019 to oversee the Age of Empires series.

Unfortunately, World’s Edge was hit hard by the latest job cuts. According to a post by former creative director Adam Isgreen on ResetEra, Xbox let go of just under half the studio, including Isgreen. On top of this, software engineer Andrew Martz wrote on LinkedIn that, as part of the reorganization, Microsoft canceled its next project. Given that World’s Edge was created to oversee the Age of Empires series, the canceled title was probably a new game in the franchise (or perhaps a spinoff like Age of Mythology ). In Martz’s case, he was laid off just seven days after receiving a promotion. “I guess it is time to pick up the pieces one more time,” he wrote in the post announcing the news.
points: Xbox 's ongoing layoffs are so sweeping that we’re still piecing together the full picture.

articles.title: Bethesda Ditches Divisive Quake Game's Free-To-Play Model in Final Update
articles.summary: Bethesda Softworks and id Software have released patch 1.31 for Quake Champions, but it turns out this will likely be the game's last update. The official patch notes reveal that "no additional content updates are planned at this time" as the game moves into a "new chapter." This marks the end of…
body: The biggest change coming to the game revolves around its payment model. Since 2018, Quake Champions has been free-to-play, meaning that anyone can download and play the title. Going forward, the game will be a paid title exclusively available on Steam for $9.99. If you previously played Quake Champions on Steam, the new paid version will be available at no additional cost. Those who played the game through the Microsoft Store will need to link their Bethesda.net account to their Steam account to gain access to the new version, though Bethesda warns that this service will only be available until Oct. 7.

id Software is a subsidiary of ZeniMax Media, the owner of Bethesda Softworks; ZeniMax was acquired by Microsoft in 2021 and now operates within Microsoft's Xbox division. In recent months, Xbox has undergone several rounds of layoffs, studio closures, and game cancellations. Unfortunately, id Software did not escape unscathed.

I spend almost six hours ranking up to level 31+ in Act One, chugging along even when I become braindead and frustrated, promising myself that the next day will be better, that I'll finally complete the puzzles I'm working on between making negronis and fetching towels. articles.title: Capcom Officially Just Let Down Millions of Gamers
articles.summary: This year's Tokyo Game Show has come and gone, and with it another sterling opportunity for an Ace Attorney 7 announcement. But fans got a flurry of hope earlier this week — followed by yet another wave of disappointment. On Wednesday, Capcom announced a VR port of the fifth game in the series.
body: Don't get me wrong — Ace Attorney will probably be pretty great in VR. The controls aren't too complicated or twitchy, and investigations would only be enhanced with greater immersion. That said, the last new entry in the Ace Attorney series was 2017's delightful The Great Ace Attorney 2: Resolve. Set in London during the 19th century, both two Great Ace Attorney games were eventually released outside Japan in 2021. Though there have been plenty of Ace Attorney ports to various platforms since 2017, it's been nearly a decade since fans have gotten new cases to pore over. And they've made their dismay clear on social media after this week's announcement.

"Quickest excited to disappointed I’ve experienced in my life," wrote one X user in response to the news. "Immediately jumped out of my seat and then actually read the whole tweet," said another forlorn fan on X.
points: This year's Tokyo Game Show has come and gone, and with it another sterling opportunity for an Ace Attorney 7 announcement.

articles.title: "I assume someone is being greedy somewhere" - Tim Schafer discusses current game industry woes following Double Fine's split with Xbox
articles.summary: Tim Schafer - the founder of acclaimed developer Double Fine Productions, and the legendary designer behind the likes of Day of the Tentacle and Psychonauts - has spoken out about his studio's recent shift to independence, as well as Game Pass, and industry woes at large.
body: In an interview with the BBC, Schafer was asked what changes at Xbox had, to his mind, resulted in Microsoft jettisoning his San Francisco-based studio. "Our mission in the beginning - seven years ago - was to really support Game Pass and fill it with as much goodness as we could," he replied. "We put our back catalogue and new stuff, about 13 games on Game Pass.

Their model I think is changing. They're going in a different direction with fewer, larger IPs. So our technique of making a lot of little IPs isn't aligned with that. We wanted to keep doing that, so we went our separate ways."

When asked what he thought about Game Pass now, and the subscription service's sustainability, Schafer said: "I love it as an idea. I liked it for Double Fine games. If you're sitting in a store and holding a disc, and it costs $70, and it's about a walking lighthouse, there's a barrier there. But if you've just got to download a game you've already paid for, it might lead people to trying weird games like Double Fine makes. So I'm very pro Game Pass, and hope it succeeds and goes forward."

articles.title: Quake Champions ditches free-to-play and kills off its Microsoft Store version eight years after its original release
articles.summary: In an unusual move, developer id Software's free-to-play shooter Quake Champions is transitioning into a paid product, eight years after its original release. As part of the same move, the Microsoft studio is killing off the Microsoft Store version, meaning it's now only available on Steam.
body: Quake Champions' new paid version costs £8.99/$9.99 and includes content from the 30 seasons released over the years. What's more, all Champions - the game's hero characters - are unlocked for everyone to use, and most cosmetic items are available for all to equip too. Unfortunately, this transition also marks the end of ongoing development. "No additional content updates are planned at this time," id Software confirmed on Steam.

Quake Champions' new - and final - chapter kicks off with patch 1.31, and sees the removal of battle passes, the in-game store, paid currencies, loot boxes, login rewards, and all microtransactions. It also reorganises the UI to remove various free-to-play tabs and sections, with character customisation now more prominent on the main menu.

Initially released in paid early access in 2017, Quake Champions was seen as something of a live-service experiment by id Software. It went free-to-play in 2018 and got its full release in 2022, following numerous updates which added new characters, weapons, and so many vanity items inspired by id Software's history.
points: In an unusual move, developer id Software's free-to-play shooter Quake Champions is transitioning into a paid product, eight years after its original release.
